title: Cluster 01 DRILL: Cell Signalling
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 3 · 8 questions · 130 marks · 19 parts · built on LOs 3(m), 3(n), 3(o) and 3(p) only
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b); that is the point of the layout.

Rate your confidence before every reveal. A dashed line sits above each answer block. Say high, medium or guessed out loud before you click. A correct guess is not mastery, and the transcript needs to record which is which, because a right answer said hesitantly stays ACTIVE while a right answer said confidently moves on.

Eight questions, and eight is what the coverage produced. Cluster 1 carries exactly four learning outcomes, 3(m), 3(n), 3(o) and 3(p), and the study sheet teaches nine sections under them. Grouped by the concept that has to surface, those collapse into eight questions, each fusing at least five concepts. A ninth would have to repeat a primary concept, so there is no ninth. Nothing here is padding.

Question 2 is the one that matters most. 9477 Specimen Paper 1 Q22 prints a five-stage pathway and asks which stages show signal amplification and which show enzyme activation. Amplification is where one molecule causes many to be produced. Activation is where a molecule is switched on. They are different steps, chapter 3.1 never separates them, and if you have only learnt that cascades amplify you cannot answer it. Q2 gives you the real specimen diagram, then makes you count the amplification steps in a second cascade, then breaks the condition that makes amplification possible.

Seven of the eight questions open on a real figure or a real data table, because 38.3% of the 684 questions in the cell-signalling corpus are figure-led and data interpretation is the largest single archetype in Book 3. Every image is the actual picture from the paper or chapter it came from, not a redrawing. Two questions are multiple choice, Q2(a) and Q6(a), and in both you have to say whether every row is right and why, not find the odd one out. The letter on its own is worth almost nothing.

Reaches back into Books 1 and 2. Q1(a) sets a receptor against an enzyme, so the whole question needs Book 1 cold. Q1(b) needs hydrophobic R groups forming hydrophobic interactions with the fatty acid tails. Q5(a) needs membrane fluidity. Q6(a) needs a transcription activator from Book 2. Q8(a) and Q8(b) need Book 2's control of gene expression, because LO 3(m) words the cellular response as a change in gene expression. A Book 1 or Book 2 gap surfacing here is worth more than a clean Book 3 answer, so say it out loud when it happens.

Scope, so you do not waste an answer. Homeostasis, negative feedback, set point and diabetes all return zero hits in the 9477 syllabus, and 22.8% of the cell-signalling question bank tests those or tests excluded receptors. Nothing here does. Intracellular receptors are excluded in the wording of LO 3(m), so only two receptor types appear anywhere in this drill: the G-protein linked receptor and the receptor tyrosine kinase. Nothing from chapters 3.2, 3.3 or 3.4 appears either, because you have not studied them yet.

One primary concept each, checked for duplicates. Q1 ligand–receptor interaction set against enzyme–substrate interaction · Q2 signal amplification distinguished from enzyme activation · Q3 kinases and phosphatases as a molecular switch, and signal termination · Q4 the nature and roles of second messengers · Q5 the G-protein switch and the GPLR working principle · Q6 receptor tyrosine kinase activation, and GPLR against RTK point for point · Q7 insulin and glucagon regulating blood glucose through their two receptor classes · Q8 the cellular response as a change in gene expression, and why two cells differ. No concept is the primary target of two questions.

Traps deliberately planted, every one traceable to a real reject line, examiner comment or specimen question. Amplification confused with activation, which is Specimen P1 Q22 exactly. The GDP said to be phosphorylated to become GTP, which is the most repeated reject in this chapter's corpus. A receptor's binding site called an active site, and the enzyme vocabulary that follows it. Phosphorylation assumed always to activate, when the chapter's own figure has protein kinase A phosphorylating glycogen synthase to inhibit it. Yes/no comparisons of the two receptor types, rejected in writing by two schemes. Tyrosine kinase used interchangeably with tyrosine residue. Cyclic AMP treated as a ligand for a cell surface receptor, which caught over 40% of one cohort. Glucagon said to act on skeletal muscle, which is your own chapter's error on pages 36, 37 and 41. A data answer given without quoting the data.
